measurement_method: TTFT measured from Ollama generate API response (time from request send to first token received)

qwen2.5-coder:7b-instruct-q3_K_M (M1).note: Primary coding engine - highest TTFT due to 7B model size. Keep-alive helps but model is inherently slower to start generating.

ornith-9b-iq3m-4k:latest (M1).note: Architectural reasoning - excellent TTFT when warm (1s), degrades on queue contention (18s).

qwen2.5-coder:3b (HP).note: Secondary coding - best TTFT when warm (703ms). Cold arrival penalty (17s) due to network + model load from HP Ollama.

cold_ttft_benchmark.description: TTFT when model is not resident in VRAM (cold start)

ttft_optimizations_applied.name: Warm model preload
ttft_optimizations_applied.effect: Models loaded into VRAM before runs. Eliminates cold-start TTFT for first call.

ttft_optimizations_applied.name: Keep-alive inference calls
ttft_optimizations_applied.effect: Models stay resident between calls. Prevents cold-start TTFT on subsequent calls within a run.

ttft_reduction.before_warm: First-call TTFT would be ~5-18s cold depending on model and machine
ttft_reduction.after_warm: First-call TTFT: ~1-2s for ornith-9b, ~700ms for qwen3b, ~38-55s for qwen7b (inherent model size)
ttft_reduction.remaining_ttft_bottleneck: qwen7b on M1 has inherently high TTFT (38-55s) due to 7B model size. This is the single largest TTFT contributor.

conclusion: TTFT optimization focused on eliminating cold-start penalties (OPT-2, OPT-3). Remaining TTFT bottleneck is qwen7b's inherent 38-55s first-token latency on M1. This is a model-size limitation, not an optimization gap. ornith-9b and qwen3b have acceptable warm TTFT.
